subject: Private deployment SLA: attribution for customer-managed edge/egress
messages:
From: Alec Chen <alec.chen@heliohealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira.patel@heliohealth.com>
Date: 2028-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed latency spikes on Private deployment — need attribution guidance

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing periodic tail-latency spikes (p99 ~ 1.2s) on our private deployment in us-west-2 since we brought the edge NAT and egress filtering under our control. The spikes line up with a handful of days where our ops pushed new firewall rules.

Can you confirm how Redwood attributes uptime/latency responsibility when the customer manages perimeter networking (NAT, firewall, edge proxies)? HelioHealth's SREs need to know whether we request a carveout vs submit evidence for attribution.

I've attached a small sample (latency-sample-20280801.csv) and a short tcpdump trace (network-trace-20280801.txt). We want to avoid an SLA breach on your side if the root cause is clearly on our edge.

Thanks — would appreciate a clear path and any required evidence format.

Best,
Alec Chen
Director of Infrastructure, HelioHealth

Attachments: latency-sample-20280801.csv (CSV, 28KB); network-trace-20280801.txt (log, 1.2MB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Chen <alec.chen@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes on Private deployment — need attribution guidance

Hi Alec — thanks for the samples and the heads up.

Short answer: we can accept evidence-based attribution when customers manage edge/networking, but we need a compact evidence bundle and a brief appendix to the SLA that defines the criteria for attribution.

What we'd like from HelioHealth to evaluate an incident:
- A short timeline of the incident (UTC) and the exact timestamps you believe the edge change occurred.
- Packet captures or flow logs (pcap, or a 60s trimmed tcpdump) aligned to the timeline.
- Metrics from your edge proxy / firewall showing request/egress latencies and rule-change audit logs.
- Any correlation showing retries/timeouts from your side.

Operationally, we typically propose a 3-part approach:
1) Evidence submission: you send the bundle (we'll treat it as confidential).
2) Joint triage: our infra + yours analyze within 3 business days.
3) Attribution decision: if evidence shows customer-side cause per the appendix criteria, Redwood will record a non-attributable event and not count it against our uptime/latency SLO; otherwise it remains Redwood responsibility.

I'll loop Jonas and Marissa for the appendix language and a draft we can attach to the private deployment agreement. If this is acceptable, we can do a 30-minute sync tomorrow to go over sample evidence format.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
---
Note: Please add any additional evidence types we should accept (e.g., BPF traces).

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Alec Chen <alec.chen@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-05T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes on Private deployment — need attribution guidance

Alec / team — quick technical note and a draft appendix attached.

Technical points:
- In customer-managed-edge scenarios we need correlated signs that requests fail or queue before they reach our edge (tcp retransmits, SYN retries, firewall rule hit counts). If the pcap shows the SYN handshake completes and our server responds with higher service time, that's Redwood. If the pcap shows the connection is delayed/blocked at customer egress, that's HelioHealth.
- For latency-only SLOs (p95/p99), we accept either packet-level traces or a combination of flow logs + edge-proxy metrics with matching timestamps.

I've attached a draft appendix "cust-managed-edge-appendix-draft.docx" that contains:
- A short incident evidence checklist (format, timestamps, trimming guidance)
- A definition of "customer-managed edge" and accepted carveouts
- A decision matrix for borderline cases

If you want, we can push this appendix into DocuSign once both sides sign off.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cust-managed-edge-appendix-draft.docx (docx, 46KB)

Thanks Kimberly and Jonas — this is helpful. Samira (procurement) is now copied — she'll want the specific SLA language we can include in our contract so legal can approve.

Two quick asks from HelioHealth:
1) Can Redwood confirm that evidence submitted for attribution will be accepted as primary and not require an extended escrow or third-party witness?
2) Will accepting the carveout affect the baseline for our monthly uptime reporting or the billing credit calculations?

I'll review the draft appendix and loop back with any redlines. If we can agree on wording this week, procurement will move the redline to DocuSign.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed latency spikes on Private deployment — need attribution guidance

Alec / Samira —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. To answer your two asks:

1) Evidence acceptance: yes — Redwood will treat an evidence bundle (as defined in the appendix) as the primary basis for attribution. We do not require a third-party witness by default. In borderline cases where datasets conflict, we agree a joint replay session (our engineers + yours) within 5 business days; if both parties still disagree, the standard escalation path applies (neutral reviewer clause).

2) Billing and reporting: attribution carveouts will be recorded as non-attributable events and will not count against Redwood uptime reporting. For billing credits, we will exclude non-attributable incidents from credit calculations — i.e., if an incident is attributed to customer-managed-edge per the appendix, it will not trigger credits. We'll surface the event in the monthly incident feed with a short rationale.

Proposed contract clause (draft snippet you can paste into an addendum):
"When Customer manages perimeter networking (hereafter, "Customer-Managed Edge") and provides an evidence bundle that satisfies the Appendix "Customer-Managed Edge Evidence" requirements, Redwood will treat the incident as non-attributable to Redwood for purposes of uptime and latency SLO calculations. The evidence bundle shall include timestamps, trimmed packet captures or flow logs, and change-audit logs from Customer systems. Both parties agree to a joint triage within 3 business days of evidence submission."

Next steps:
- Jonas / Marissa: if the appendix looks good, please finalize and upload to DocuSign (link: https://www.docusign.com/hellodocs/HL-0427-edge-appendix).
- HelioHealth: send a redline if you need alternate wording — we can do a quick legal-to-legal call.
- Optional: we recommend a 30-day baseline after the appendix is signed where we collect an initial latency baseline (no credits during baseline) so we both have a clean comparison.

I've attached a short proposed addendum PDF for your legal team: proposed-sla-addendum-heliohealth.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-sla-addendum-heliohealth.pdf (pdf, 12KB)
